Functions, domain and range: A function gives each input exactly one output. The domain is the set of allowed inputs and the range is the set of outputs. A graph is a function if no vertical line crosses it twice. To evaluate f(x), replace x with the input, using parentheses for expressions and negative numbers. To find a domain, remove inputs that cause division by zero or a square root of a negative number.
Parent functions: A parent function is the simplest member of a family: constant, linear, x^2, x^3, absolute value, square root and 1/x. Know the shape, domain and range of each. Even functions such as x^2 are symmetric about the y-axis, since f(-x) = f(x). Odd functions such as x^3 and 1/x are symmetric about the origin, since f(-x) = -f(x). The graph of 1/x has a vertical asymptote at x = 0 and a horizontal asymptote at y = 0.
Transformations of functions: Adding k outside, f(x) + k, moves the graph up k. Subtracting h inside, f(x - h), moves it right h, and f(x + 4) moves it left 4. The expression -f(x) reflects over the x-axis and f(-x) reflects over the y-axis. A factor a with a > 1 stretches vertically and 0 < a < 1 shrinks. In vertex form y = a(x - h)^2 + k the vertex is (h, k). Do stretches and reflections before shifts.
Absolute value and piecewise functions: The absolute value of a number is its distance from 0. If abs(u) = c with c > 0, then u = c or u = -c. If abs(u) < c, then -c < u < c (and). If abs(u) > c, then u < -c or u > c (or). Check answers when the other side has a variable, since some can be extraneous. The graph of y = a*abs(x - h) + k is a V with vertex (h, k). A piecewise function uses different rules on different intervals, so find the interval first.
Combining functions and composition: Functions can be added, subtracted, multiplied and divided: (f + g)(x) = f(x) + g(x), and for a quotient g(x) cannot be 0. The composition (f o g)(x) = f(g(x)) applies g first and then f. Order matters, so f(g(x)) is usually different from g(f(x)). The domain of a composition needs x to be in the domain of the inside function and the inside output to be in the domain of the outside function.
Inverse functions: The inverse f^-1 undoes f: f(a) = b means f^-1(b) = a. An inverse function exists only if f is one-to-one (it passes the horizontal line test). To find it, write y = f(x), swap x and y, and solve for y. Functions f and g are inverses if f(g(x)) = x and g(f(x)) = x. The graph of f^-1 is the reflection of f over y = x, and the domain and range swap. The notation f^-1 does not mean 1/f.
